abstract: The Na+/H+ exchanger is a ubiquitous plasma membrane protein that is responsible for pH regulation and is activated by growth factors. We examined the role of the Na+/H+ exchanger in cell growth and differentiation. Treatment of P19 cells with the Na+/H+ exchanger inhibitor Hoe 694 eliminated retinoic acid-induced differentiation in this cell line. We developed a P19 embryonal carcinoma cell line that was deficient in the Na+/H+ antiporter. Na+/H+ exchanger-deficient cells were reduced in the rate of cell growth and this effect was enhanced by the removal of added HCO3- and by reducing extracellular pH. The antiporter-deficient cells were also markedly deficient in their ability to differentiate to neuronal-like cells and recovered this ability when the Na+/H+ antiporter was reintroduced. The results show that the absence of Na+/H+ antiport as a pH regulatory mechanism can result in deficiencies in both cell growth and differentiation in embryonal carcinoma cells.
abstract_ja: Na+/H+交換体は、細胞膜に広く存在するタンパク質で、pH調節を担い、増殖因子によって活性化されます。我々は、細胞の増殖と分化における役割を検討しました。Na+/H+交換体阻害剤Hoe 694でP19細胞を処理すると、レチノイン酸誘導性分化が消失しました。Na+/H+交換体を欠損させたP19胎児性癌細胞株を作製したところ、細胞増殖速度が低下し、この低下は培地からHCO3-を除去したり細胞外pHを下げたりすると増強されました。欠損細胞は神経様細胞への分化能も著しく低下しましたが、Na+/H+アンチポーターを再導入すると分化能が回復しました。これらの結果から、pH調節機構としてのNa+/H+アンチポーターが欠如すると、胎児性癌細胞の増殖と分化の両方に欠陥が生じることが示されました。
